title: ShortSeq: A benchmark for foundation model evaluation on short time series
description:
ShortSeq evaluates classical, machine-learning, and foundation-model forecasters on short time series, where the sample sizes that favour large pretrained models are absent.

It provides a pip-installable package (shortseq), a rolling one-step-ahead evaluation protocol with no look-ahead, and statistical significance testing: Diebold-Mariano with Bonferroni correction for pairwise per-series comparisons, and a Friedman omnibus test with Nemenyi post-hoc for ranking multiple models across series.

The benchmark comprises 368 series, split into a short stratum (n < 200, 199 series) and a long stratum (n ≥ 200, 169 series). The two strata are analysed separately and never pooled, because they exhibit opposite-signed effects at the small-model end. Of the 368, 366 are real series drawn from at most eight distinct upstream providers and 2 are seeded simulations retained for continuity with an earlier study. The ten dataset keys in the registry are not ten independent sources: two are simulated, two cover a single M-competition, and one Kaggle release is held as two non-independent views (one is the other summed across stores).

Scope and licensing. ShortSeq contributes dataset loaders, evaluation code, and computed results, and additionally distributes derived (aggregated or column-selected) series for several sources. Upstream licensing is partially established: UCI Online Retail and M3 Monthly are confirmed CC BY 4.0 and attributed accordingly; the M4 series rest on a source that states no licence at all; and three Kaggle competition sources (Rossmann, Walmart Recruiting, Store Sales) remain unverified because their rules pages require login. Kaggle's standard rules template restricts redistribution of competition data, so users should treat those three as of uncertain licensing status. The MIT licence attached to this record covers the software only.

DATASHEET.md in the repository documents composition, provenance, preprocessing, known defects, and intended and discouraged uses in full, including a per-source licensing table (section 6.2) and an erratum of known open items (section 7).
